name: Gregor Muller
profile: Austrian entrepreneur who co-founded online/hybrid tutoring platform GoStudent in Vienna in 2016 with CEO Felix Ohswald. GoStudent has raised over EUR 675m (Prosus, SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Left Lane) at a peak valuation around EUR 3bn, and has expanded via acquisitions (Seneca Learning, Tus Media, Studienkreis, Berlitz Germany sites).
interesting_fact: GoStudent Group reported its first full year of operational profitability in 2025, after a period of rapid post-pandemic expansion and restructuring.
deep_cut_fact: Before it was a platform, GoStudent began in 2016 as a WhatsApp chat through which pupils could go over their homework with tutors.
notes: Common name: a different Gregor Mueller (health economist, Thieme RECOM) exists - don't confuse. Lower public profile than CEO Felix Ohswald; GoStudent press office is best route.

name: Ben Christensen
profile: Michigan Tech alum ('14) who co-founded Handshake, the college-to-career recruiting network, with Garrett Lord and Scott Ringwelski in Houghton, Michigan. Handshake now connects ~20M students and alumni with 1M+ employers (valued ~$3.5bn) and has pushed into supplying expert talent for AI training work.
interesting_fact: Christensen nearly took a cybersecurity job at a Michigan company instead; the founders gave themselves three years to sign five schools or give up.
deep_cut_fact: He met Garrett Lord in a Michigan Tech outdoor adventure group; on early sales trips they often slept in a Ford Focus in McDonald's parking lots and once drove to Virginia and back for a single school visit.
notes: Low-profile co-founder (Crunchbase lists Denver base; previously Arbor Networks ASERT security research). Press office or Michigan Tech alumni connection are natural routes.

name: Charles Hearn
profile: Engineer who co-founded Alloy in 2015 with Tommy Nicholas and Laura Spiekerman; Alloy's identity-decisioning and fraud-prevention platform connects banks and fintechs to KYC/AML data sources and is used by 900+ financial institutions. As CTO he built the platform on AWS and still leads engineering.
interesting_fact: Named to the Forbes 30 Under 30 list in 2020; Alloy's platform architecture he led has been profiled by AWS Startups.
deep_cut_fact: Before Alloy he was a program manager at Microsoft and then lead product engineer at a payments startup (a high-risk payment processor), where he first met his future co-founders.
notes: Technical, low-profile co-founder; Alloy comms (Kylee Sibilia, listed as media contact on press releases) is the route.
